_README: THE ONE PLACE THE PUBLISHED TIMES ARE STATED. Edit here, nowhere else.
Before this file existed the times were literal strings in the HTML, the email and the
bot, and they drifted apart without anyone noticing: on 2026-08-01 the site's hero said
7:50 while the same page's how-it-works said 8:05, outro.html said 8:05, the Telegram bot
said 8:30 and the subscriber email said ~8:05. Four different promises, all live at once.
Site pages render these into any element carrying data-schedule="<key>". The element's
existing text is the fallback, so a failed fetch degrades to the last shipped value
instead of a blank. Python consumers (email, bot) read the same file via publish_schedule.py.
check_published_times.py fails if any consumer states a clock time this file does not.
RULE: these are PROMISES TO CUSTOMERS, not internal job times. Only widen them toward
honesty. 'card' is 8:45 rather than 8:30 because the measured send on 2026-08-01 was
08:37 — promising 8:30 would ship a claim we already know we miss.

2026-08-09 — THE FIXED PROMISE IS WITHDRAWN. Node 0: the 7:50/8:05 times were arbitrary, chosen months ago for an NBA-only product and kept because they had been promised and imposed discipline on manual work. Delivery is READY-BASED now: the free pick ships when the data is in, timed to leave the customer room to act. Measured fires were 08:08 PT (08-07) and 09:52 PT (08-08) - nearly two hours apart - so 7:50 was a claim we already knew we missed daily. Widened to 'by 10:00 AM PT' per this file's own rule, and the wording changed from 'posts at' to 'posts by'. NEXT STEP (task site-timing-promise-is-stale): replace the static window entirely with the ACTUAL delivery time once fired plus a dynamic estimate for today and tomorrow, from tracked timing. An estimate that tightens as we improve earns trust; a promise we miss spends it.
free_pick_sentence: The free pick posts when the day's data is in, by 10:00 AM PT.
card_sentence: The full card follows the free pick, by 10:30 AM PT.
combined_label: Free pick when the data is in · by 10:00 AM PT

_machine._note: Wall-clock OUTER BOUND the drift check compares actual delivery against - not a target. Delivery is data-gated and ready-based; measured fires ranged 08:08 to 09:52 PT. These are the times a customer was promised and must not be embarrassed by.
